alex: FYI hitting an odd edge-only failure on Vercel preview when using the JS SDK in Next middleware: "TypeError: fetch is not a function" even though it works locally.
yara: That usually means SWC bundled a node shim or the wrong entrypoint. If bundler resolves to the CJS build it can pull in node shims that break worker globals.
yara: Quick check: inspect the built preview bundle. If you see imports for 'util' or 'fs' that's a red flag.
miles: We had a race where top-level logger import pulled in `util.inspect` and SWC serialized it into the edge bundle. Fix was to lazy-init node logger behind a runtime check so edge customers never bundle it.
miles: Pattern we use: `if (typeof process !== 'undefined' && process.release?.name === 'node') { await import('./node-only') }`
alex: Moving client creation inside middleware helped in my case, but TS still flags `Request`/`Response` as unknown types when compiling middleware.
lin: For TS, two good levers: 1) ship an edge-specific d.ts that references DOM libs only, 2) document a minimal tsconfig for middleware with "lib": ["esnext","dom"]. We landed both.
lin: Also, remove Node types from the main public types (no Buffer, NodeJS.Timer). Provide node-only augmentations in a separate file.
yara: Packaging note: add explicit exports map so edge consumers resolve "./edge" entry. Example: "exports": { ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},"./edge":"./dist/edge.mjs" }
miles: Runtime gotcha: retry/backoff using setTimeout breaks on worker-style edges. Replace with AbortController/timeouts or `signal.timeout` when available.
ci-bot: ci/test:edge-sanity failed: missing ./edge export in package.json.
yara: Plan: small patch to 1) emit dist/edge.mjs, 2) publish dist/edge.d.ts (web types), 3) lazy-load node-only modules, 4) replace timer-based retry, 5) add examples/nextjs-edge-middleware. Target: hotfix release tomorrow.
alex: Thanks — I can validate on the preview and attach a minimal repro. :thumbsup:
